what: The delegated delta review of the I62 instrument (spec/M2/lib/mutation_catalog_i62.json: a rerun of I61's 242-mutant catalog with I61's defects D1-D8 fixed) and of its fixes (a233867..25a29ac, plus 9c825ad and 929fa41), under both lenses.
who: One fresh, independent agent, delegated by the lead to hold both the fairness and the soundness lens (instrument adjudication.review, Step 1: one fresh agent, both lenses). It drafted nothing of I62. It saw no forecast, no I62 test, prompt or result, and no I61 result or report beyond what the instrument states.

advisory: replaces.carried says that computation, pins, ..., projection, ... are I61's 'byte for byte'. Two of the listed fields are not. The instrument is json.dumps(indent=1) of insertion-ordered keys, so I serialized each of the 27 fields that list names the same way. 25 are byte-identical to I61's. pins differs: pins.why gains a sentence, and pins.i61_pipeline_commit is new. projection differs: projection.output now names gen/M2/mutation_i62/header.projected.json. Everything that decides something is unchanged: pins.files, pins.holon_commit, pins.i60_holon_commit and every projection rule. gen/M2/mutation_i62/header.projected.json is byte-identical to I61's (sha256 e2cd5549...), and `holon mutate project --check` reproduces it under key I62. Fix: the report should say 'unchanged except the I62 output path and a note', not 'byte for byte'.

Nothing in the code checks that the equivalence verdicts are carried. adjudication.file requires spec/M2/equivalent_mutants_i62.json to be I61's file with every verdict I61's (equivalent, reason, duplicate_of, panel), and its delegation to name I61's decision, panel, procedure and blindness_audit. holon/mutate/run.py check_adjudication checks only the instrument ref, mutants_sha256, diff_sheet_sha256, the review ref and the completeness of the ids. A changed verdict would therefore pass the catalog-run precondition. Fix: before any catalog record, compare every verdict with spec/M2/equivalent_mutants_i61.json byte for byte, and check the delegation fields. This can go in the precondition or in the contract. The carry itself is sound; see 'checked'.

The forecast is not blind, and the instrument says so (limitations[14], harness_gate.before_prereg). It was made after I61's run, and after the lead ran the fixed code on catalog mutants: A001 (the 16 hits of each round-trip law), A076 and A116, plus the header width law of a kept A116 tree. So the I62 predictions test whether the fixes do what they claim; they do not test the catalog's sensitivity afresh. This does not make the rate unfair, because the catalog, the kill criterion and the code are all fixed before the run. The report should keep this caveat next to every I62 prediction it scores.

The human decision that replaces.rule cites is not in docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md. replaces.rule says 'The human chose it (the I61 PR's questions: a new key and rerun, the gate rule, the I20 harness, the header ledger bundle)'. docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md has no I61/I62 entry; its latest entry is Q38 (F35). I did not read docs/iterations/I61.md, which may hold the decision. Fix: record the decision in docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md, as the other decisions are, so that the provenance of the new key does not rest on a PR thread.

This sign-off covers the code at 929fa41: the diff a233867..25a29ac, plus 9c825ad and 929fa41, which the lead added after my checkout. adjudication.review asks for the diff up to 'the gate's pipeline commit, once committed'. That means any change to holon/mutate, holon/records.py, spec/M2/ledger.json, replay/M2/mutation_i62/, or any module on the M0/M1x/M2 decision path.

advisory: channels.i20_step contradicts itself for the five D2 mutants. It keeps I61's sentence 'A completed run covers at least 2432 steps (the m1 source alone)'. Under the D2 fix, a mutant whose every deployment reverts (A076, A098, A100, A101, A104) completes with steps 0, error null, and every base step id in corpus_differences (channels.py i20_mutant: entry(I20, len(r.compared), ...)). I61's contract asserts steps >= 2432 for every completed i20_step run (tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy_i61.py:2226-2227). If I62's contract keeps that assertion (I did not read it), those five records will fail it. No kill depends on this, because channels never decide one. Fix: state that the 2432-step floor holds only for runs whose deployments succeed, and have the contract assert it only there.

No check certifies the D2 copies on the original code. D7 fails the gate only on a replay disagreement or an error of step 'replay'. A copy that silently made every trace 'hold' would pass the gate, for example one whose probe always reverts. It would also pass the baseline precondition, which compares statuses only. From the diff, I find the copies equivalent to I20's and I15's files wherever the deployment succeeds: the probe's state is reverted from a snapshot (the test contract's storage, nonces and balances), so the deployed addresses and the T, K, Q and 'S d' lines are the same; recordLogs restarts before every call; state-diff recording is off during the probe; the probe's only extra output is a second console line 'HOLON-HDR <tid> g 0 ...', which nothing parses. The step harness reads only HOLON_STEPS_OUT, and holon.mutate.replay._trace_outcomes reads only mreplay.LINE ('HOLON (\d+) (\d+) (ok|rev)'). That is reasoning, not a test. Fix, cheap and before any catalog mutant runs: the I62 baseline's gen/M2/mutation_i62/i20_corpus.json must equal I61's gen/M2/mutation_i61/i20_corpus.json byte for byte, which it should, since the corpus code is unchanged since a233867. Likewise, the I62 baseline record's trace-replay outcomes must equal I61's. One more risk is caught already: the trace harness is gas-metered (I15 chunks traces 'to stay under the block gas limit'), and the probe doubles each trace's deployment gas. Any failure from that would surface as a step-'replay' error on the controls, which D7 catches.

Still open from I61's soundness review: a failed replay is filed as a replay disagreement, not as an error. decide_m0 (run.py:568-577) and trace_replay (run.py:755-768) set replay to null and log a step-'replay' error that names no law. decide.how (decide.py:33-50) then files a law that moved to REFUTED as replay_disagreement. That sets extraction_defect_detected and the survivor class extraction_gap/replay, and the outcome is never 'error'. D1 in I61 was exactly this case. D7 now stops the run when it happens on a control. On a catalog mutant it would still be recorded only as a flag and a class. The rates are unaffected, because an error and a survivor both count as not killed, but the flag and the class would be wrong. Fix: a law whose replay fails gets error for its K1 determination, never replay_disagreement.

D7 is narrower than its own reason, 'the replay harness is what the gate certifies'. gate_controls (run.py:1469-1470) fails a control only on rec.replay_disagreements or on an error of step 'replay'. These still pass: an error of step 'falsifier', even though the K2 (c) search runs the same harness through unit_claims and original_claims; and an error of step 'counter_law', 'proof_check', 'M0', 'M1x', 'M2' or 'unit' on a control that is still killed as expected. For example, C4 also loses L_par_hdr_v1's proof besides L_rt_go_v1/v2, so it runs a third K2 (c) search, and an error there would pass. Fix: fail the controls check on any error in a control's record, or at least on 'falsifier' errors too.

D8 is a rule only; the code does not enforce it. Nothing refuses `holon mutate replay --i16` (the i16 check itself) or `holon mutate run --control C1..C4` (the controls check) before the gate's first attempt: cmd_run needs only a clean tree and a baseline record. gate.json records attempts, so it cannot show that no rehearsal took place. I61's contract class TestReplayHarness runs `holon mutate replay --i16` (tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy_i61.py:1675). If I62's contract keeps that class, running the contract on the build before the first attempt would be a partial rehearsal. The 929fa41 commit message records that the contract's TestOperators ran on the build; that is a static check, not a gate check. Fix: list the contract classes that may run before the first attempt, and record in the attempt every command run on the build beforehand. Alternatively, make the first attempt the first execution, from a fresh CI checkout.

D4 applies only to the M2 set run (run.py:977-1009), as kill_criterion.errors says. decide_m0 (`holon run --milestone M0`, run.py:535-547) and decide_m1x (`holon differential`, run.py:846-856) still mark every law of their set error when the set run fails twice. So 'Errors are scoped to laws' still has two set-level exceptions; say so. D4 cannot create a kill at this pipeline. M2 SORT-site laws are decided on the hand model, and every return path of holon/sorts/width.py decide is UNKNOWN. So D4 can only isolate errors.

Two gaps in D6's determinism. First, channel errors. channels.error_text (channels.py:139-166) replaces only its own places (holon, tree, work, code, sol_deps) before it cuts the message to 400 characters. Home, interpreter and pinned-checkout paths are replaced only later, by run_unit's final C.scrub pass (run.py:1172-1179). A channel error that quotes such a path in its first 400 characters therefore still cuts at a place that depends on the machine. This contradicts reporting.determinism ('scrubbed before it is cut'). Second, a step retried by _retry or _channel_retry leaves no trace of its first failure in the record. Neither gap affects a decision.

D3's coverage rule is broader than the defect. holon/records.py:499-504 returns null coverage for every *.extracted.json document that the coverage report does not list and whose extraction.kind is not 'transitions'. That is all six non-rollup documents in spec/M2/facts: the five Go documents as well as the header. It is harmless today: coverage is a record field, not a decision input, and the only law over those documents in the mutation run is the D3 width law.

F35 does not change a decision rule of the M0, M1x or M2 pipeline. bend.run (bend.py:271-302) returns the same Run as before, with the same default bounds: the same exit code and stdout+stderr for a completed check, and code None with '[timeout]' for a timeout. The checker now starts in its own session, and on a timeout or an exception its whole process group is killed, as run_budgeted already did. check() and check_verdict() gain an optional timeout whose default is unchanged. holon/gen/equivalence.py, holon/gen/eqsearch.py, holon/statement_diff.py and config 'equivalence' are reached only from M3 binding-change proofs, from G2, and from holon/gate.py's statement-diff scan, which F35 scoped to the gate's milestone. They are never reached from holon run, derive, model, differential, extract or the channel library calls; mpipeline uses only bindings.defs_index, dependents, kernel_cone and kernel_entries. F35's changes to the M0-M2 records are generator_sha256 and timings only, field by field. So F35 can move a decision only through resources. A timed-out check no longer leaves BendTT or Lean children running, so a later check in the same unit is less likely to time out. A timeout is never a verdict (not_K2 makes it an error), so this can turn a would-be timeout error into a decided status. It cannot fabricate a refutation or a proof rejection. The instrument never names F35. reporting.first_run must explain every changed record by a defect or call it a Surprise, so F35 should be listed as a known difference between the two pipeline commits that is not a fix.

Commit order matters for the generator hashes. The 641293e message says the M1/M2 records' generator_sha256 would be regenerated 'in the next commit', but 25a29ac does not do that. At 25a29ac those committed records were stale; 9c825ad regenerated them. In the 28 records 9c825ad touches, only generator_sha256 and seconds differ, which I checked field by field. So the gate's pipeline commit must descend from 9c825ad. holon/records.py is also in the generator closures of the M3 deciders (holon/sorts/run3.GEN3, holon/disch, holon/undo), whose committed records were not regenerated. Their generator_sha256 matched none of those closures at bacec28 either, so this is no new mismatch. M3 is outside the mutation run, because gen/M3 is excluded from the scratch trees.
soundness.checked: Read: the I62 instrument in full against I61's, and I61's review (both lenses). Also the code diff a233867..25a29ac, with forbidden paths excluded: holon/mutate/{channels,common,m0,rate,replay,run,stage}.py, holon/metrics.py, holon/records.py, spec/M2/ledger.json, the two copies under replay/M2/mutation_i62/, gen/M2/mutation_i62/header.projected.json, .github/workflows/holon-i62-run.yml, and F35's files (holon/bend.py, holon/gate.py, holon/gen/equivalence.py, holon/gen/eqsearch.py, holon/statement_diff.py, config 'equivalence', laws/STATEMENT_DIFF.jsonl, whose three new lines are M3 binding_change entries). Also 9c825ad and 929fa41, in /home/user/HOLON-i61b. Also the unchanged code these rely on: holon/replay_fragments.py (harness_project, run_harness, parse_output, compare_runs, which skips the 'd' exec), holon/mreplay.py (LINE, last_step, which calls deploy() directly in setUp), holon/refute.py subterms, holon/model_eval.py value_out ('MaybeFields' none is a defined None), holon/sorts/width.py, the ledger functions of holon/records.py, holon/diagram/build.py, holon/gen/oracles.py ledger_problems (G9, per law), holon/gen/linked.py declared_bundle (it reads the documents' own assumptions), and the Go and Solidity harnesses. None of these changed between a233867 and 929fa41: git log on these paths is empty. Per defect: D1. In replay.py:1118-1194, a dec_go None result becomes NONE_VALUE, which is compared like any value. A field of none, or a role called on none, is no execution. This matches the model: refute.subterms with value_out('MaybeFields') treats none as a defined value unequal to some(...). The 8 laws/M0 statements contain no field of a call result and no role applied to dec_go's output, so those two clauses are unreachable today. The Go harness writes null only from decode when validate() fails (replay/M2/mutation_i61/holon_mutate_replay_test.go:183-186). My scratch tests of replay._Eval pass: none vs some is False; equal values are True; none == none is True; a revert is None; a panic is False; a field of none or a call on none is None and makes no call. The kills D1 can add (K1 on L_rt_go_* hits, K2 (c) falsifications) are licensed by I61's own replay.semantics ('dec_go is None when validate() errs'; 'an error or revert that is the function's value is not a violation'). I61's evaluator raised instead. D2. Diffing each copy against its original shows only the probe (holonProbeDeploy/holonDeploys, probeDeploy/deploys), the F line and the 'rev deploy' lines. I20's and I15's files are untouched. channels._run_steps (channels.py:290-332) uses the same chunks, command, environment and DONE check as run_harness. The baseline path (traces None) still calls run_harness, so a reverted deployment there leaves a trace with no run and fails the run. Every trace uses the same init, so a mutant's deployments either all revert or all succeed. compare_runs never compares the deployment exec with the model, so 'no disagreement' is accurate. trace_claims (replay.py:1087-1106) falsifies only on 'rev panic:', so a 'rev deploy: ...' step holds. Neither path can make a kill: channels never decide one; width laws are UNKNOWN on every path; M1x statuses are carried by construction and M2 site laws are decided on the hand model, so no trace law moves; and a masked obstruction needs a replay on the mutant. D3. records._meets treats '*' as always meeting the cone, so every law over the header document carries all four assumptions. unclassified ignores '*', so a derived header document whose cone is non-empty raises LedgerError. resolve_bundle's derived path needs exactly one bundle with that facts path, and the new bundle is the only one. No law in laws/M0-M3 has facts spec/M2/facts/morph_header.extracted.json. The diagram builder matches a bundle only by its own facts sha, and no diagram of that document is committed. evidence.py reads no ledger. 9c825ad: the 28 M1/M2 records differ from 25a29ac only in generator_sha256 and seconds. D4 (run.py:977-1009) matches kill_criterion.errors, and results are read only for the set that passed. D5 (run.py:1050-1060) applies to i20_baseline, i20_mutant and i16_edge, and the record keeps the second attempt's entry. D6 (common.py:51-87) is applied before every cut in run.py, stage._tail, m0.proof_attempt and the gate details, with a final pass at run.py:1172-1179. It never touches a verdict input: proof verdicts read the exit code and marker, and claims read harness values. 929fa41 rewrites the character class [\w.] as [.\w], which is the same set. Both patterns gave identical substitutions on 200,000 random strings, and scrub is idempotent. D7 is implemented in run.py:1451-1478. D8 is harness_gate.rehearsal and before_prereg, a rule only (advisory 5). Every defect, D1 to D8, has an answer. No fix can turn a mutant that I61's kill criterion leaves unkilled into a kill. D1 implements I61's stated semantics. D2, D3, D4 and D5 turn pipeline errors into decided non-kills, and D6 to D8 touch messages and the gate. Not done: I ran no mutant, control, baseline or gate, and made no bend call. My attempt to delete them was refused by the permission system. No tracked file changed: git status is clean. Every later Python run used -B and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.
